name: V-Model Regulatory Evidence Pipeline
description: Serial V-model with peer routing and one feature branch per requirement: RA defines requirements, Developer builds, QA verifies, RA accepts, and the engine merges the accepted branch into main. All git operations are mechanical (entry/exit commands); agents never run git.

REQUIREMENTS_DEFINITION.name: Requirements Definition
REQUIREMENTS_DEFINITION.description: RA writes the initial minimal requirement for a CLI application.
REQUIREMENTS_DEFINITION.prompt:
You are the Requirements Analyst. Your PRIMARY deliverable is the requirements specification document for {{requirementId}}.

You are on branch feature/{{requirementId}}; the workflow engine has already checked it out at the latest pushed commit. Do NOT run git commands (checkout, pull, commit, push, merge) -- the engine commits and pushes your work when you finish.

Work in your workspace/project directory:
1. MANDATORY: Create or update docs/requirements-specification.md -- add a new section for {{requirementId}}. The section MUST include:
   - The identifier as a heading (## {{requirementId}}: Title)
   - Requirement Identifier field
   - Title, Purpose, Scope, Out of Scope, and Traceability subsections
   - This file is the authoritative requirements record. If it does not contain {{requirementId}}, the exit gate WILL FAIL and you will be asked to redo the work.
2. Create or update docs/acceptance-criteria-checklist.md with acceptance criteria for {{requirementId}}. Each criterion must describe the product's behavior and be checkable by QA against the code. Do NOT write criteria about evidence documents (verification report, traceability matrix, acceptance verdict) -- those are produced in later states and cannot be checked before acceptance.
3. VERIFY before finishing: run `grep -q '{{requirementId}}' docs/requirements-specification.md` to confirm the identifier is present.

Keep changes focused on the single requirement in this task.

exitEvaluation.prompt: Based on the requirements definition work just completed, were BOTH of the following accomplished: (1) docs/requirements-specification.md contains a full section for {{requirementId}} (not just the checklist -- the SPECIFICATION document must have it), and (2) docs/acceptance-criteria-checklist.md created or updated with criteria for {{requirementId}}? Answer with a single word: true or false.

onEntryCommands.reason: Discard uncommitted leftovers from a prior session so the checkout below cannot be blocked.
Fetch the latest remote branches pushed by other agents.

onEntryCommands.command: git checkout -B feature/{{requirementId}} origin/feature/{{requirementId}} 2>/dev/null || git checkout -B feature/{{requirementId}} origin/{{baseBranch}}
onEntryCommands.reason: Check out the requirement's feature branch: reuse it if it was already pushed (retry), otherwise create it from {{baseBranch}}.

onExitCommands.reason: Stage all new and modified files.
Commit staged changes with the requirement ID in the message, so traceability never depends on the LLM. No-op when nothing changed.
Capture the commit SHA for downstream traceability.
Push the feature branch so the next agent can check it out.

onExitCommands.command: grep -oP 'REQ-HCDP-\d+' docs/acceptance-criteria-checklist.md | sort -u | while read req; do grep -q "$req" docs/requirements-specification.md || { echo "GATE FAIL: $req missing from docs/requirements-specification.md"; exit 1; }; done
onExitCommands.reason: Deterministic exit gate: verify every REQ-HCDP-XXX in the acceptance criteria checklist also appears in the requirements specification. If any requirement ID is missing from the spec, this command fails and the state retries with feedback.

IMPLEMENTING.name: Implementation
IMPLEMENTING.description: Developer builds the minimal CLI app per the requirement.
IMPLEMENTING.prompt:
You are the Developer. Implement {{requirementId}} as described in the task details.

You are on branch feature/{{requirementId}}; the workflow engine has already checked it out at the latest pushed commit. Do NOT run git commands (checkout, pull, commit, push, merge) -- the engine commits and pushes your work when you finish.

Work in your workspace/project directory:
1. Read docs/requirements-specification.md to understand {{requirementId}}
2. Create or update source files in src/
3. Create or update test files in tests/
4. Create test fixtures in tests/fixtures/ if needed
5. If package.json does not exist, create it (name: hcdp-validate) with tsconfig.json and jest.config.js
6. Run npm install && npx jest -- all tests must pass. The engine re-runs the tests as a gate when you finish; failing tests send the work back to you.
7. Create or update evidence/developer-traceability.md mapping {{requirementId}} to its implementation files

Keep changes focused on this task's requirement.

TypeScript strict mode: In catch blocks, the error variable is type 'unknown'. Always use 'catch (err: unknown)' and cast before accessing properties, e.g. '(err as Error).message' or guard with 'if (err instanceof Error)'.

exitEvaluation.prompt: Based on the implementation work just completed, did ALL of the following succeed: (1) source files created or updated, (2) test files created or updated, (3) all tests pass when running npx jest, and (4) evidence/developer-traceability.md updated for {{requirementId}}? Answer with a single word: true or false.

onEntryCommands.reason: Discard uncommitted leftovers from a prior session so the checkout below cannot be blocked.
Fetch the latest remote branches pushed by other agents.
Check out the requirement's feature branch exactly as last pushed. It must already exist (created in REQUIREMENTS_DEFINITION).

onExitCommands.reason: Stage all new and modified files.
Commit staged changes with the requirement ID in the message, so traceability never depends on the LLM. No-op when nothing changed.
Capture the commit SHA for downstream traceability.
Push the feature branch so the next agent can check it out.
Deterministic quality gate: all tests must pass before the work is handed off. Runs after the push, so a failure keeps the work on the feature branch and the retry continues from it.

VERIFICATION.name: QA Verification
VERIFICATION.description: QA verifies the developer's implementation against the requirements.
VERIFICATION.prompt:
You are QA. Verify the implementation of {{requirementId}} in your workspace/project directory.

You are on branch feature/{{requirementId}}; the workflow engine has already checked it out at the latest pushed commit. Do NOT run git commands (checkout, pull, commit, push, merge) -- the engine commits and pushes your work when you finish.

The engine already ran `git log --oneline --grep='{{requirementId}}' origin/{{baseBranch}}..HEAD` and captured the commits on this branch that reference the requirement:

```
{{reqCommits}}
```

The engine also ran the full test suite before you started, and it passed (a failing suite would have sent the work back to the developer).

1. Confirm the captured commits above include at least one implementation commit for {{requirementId}}. If there are none, record a FAIL for traceability.
2. Record the verified commit: run `git rev-parse HEAD` and save the hash
3. Review the source and tests against docs/requirements-specification.md and docs/acceptance-criteria-checklist.md
4. Create or update evidence/traceability-matrix.md with a row for this requirement:
   | Requirement | Implementation Commit | Tests Pass | Verified Commit | Status |
5. Create or update evidence/verification-report.md with the verified commit hash and your findings.
6. FINAL STEP, do not skip: after deciding the verdict, end the {{requirementId}} section with this exact line on its own (the engine checks it; a missing line counts as FAIL):
   QA-VERDICT {{requirementId}}: PASS
   or
   QA-VERDICT {{requirementId}}: FAIL

Scope: verify the implementation against the acceptance criteria that describe the product. A criterion about an evidence document produced in a LATER state (for example the RA's evidence/acceptance-verdict.md) is outside QA scope. Mark it N/A and do not count it against the verdict.

When updating verification, validation, or traceability reports, preserve all existing entries from prior tasks. Append new rows or sections -- do not overwrite past evidence.

You produce evidence only. You do NOT accept or merge -- acceptance is the RA's job and the engine merges after acceptance.

exitEvaluation.prompt: Look at the QA-VERDICT line you wrote for {{requirementId}} in evidence/verification-report.md. Is it exactly "QA-VERDICT {{requirementId}}: PASS"? Answer with a single word: true or false.

onEntryCommands.reason: Discard uncommitted leftovers from a prior session so the checkout below cannot be blocked.
Fetch the latest remote branches pushed by other agents.
Check out the requirement's feature branch exactly as last pushed. It must already exist (created in REQUIREMENTS_DEFINITION).
Capture the commits on this feature branch that reference {{requirementId}}, stored as reqCommits.
Deterministic gate: run the full test suite on exactly what the developer pushed. Failing tests send the work straight back to REWORK without an LLM turn.

onExitCommands.reason: Stage all new and modified files.
Commit staged changes with the requirement ID in the message, so traceability never depends on the LLM. No-op when nothing changed.
Capture the commit SHA for downstream traceability.
Push the feature branch so the next agent can check it out.

onExitCommands.command: R=evidence/verification-report.md; if grep -qE "QA-VERDICT[[:space:]]+{{requirementId}}:[[:space:]]*\\**PASS" $R && ! grep -qE "QA-VERDICT[[:space:]]+{{requirementId}}:[[:space:]]*\\**FAIL" $R; then exit 0; fi; echo "QA verdict for {{requirementId}} is not PASS. Verdict lines found:"; grep -n "QA-VERDICT" $R || echo "(none)"; echo "See $R for the QA findings."; exit 1
onExitCommands.reason: Deterministic gate: the work advances only if QA recorded an explicit PASS verdict line for this requirement. Runs after the push so the QA evidence is on the feature branch either way.

ACCEPTANCE.name: Requirements Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE.description: RA reviews QA evidence and issues final accept/reject verdict.
ACCEPTANCE.prompt:
You are the RA performing final acceptance for {{requirementId}} in your workspace/project directory.

You are on branch feature/{{requirementId}}; the workflow engine has already checked it out at the latest pushed commit. Do NOT run git commands (checkout, pull, commit, push, merge) -- the engine commits and pushes your work when you finish.

1. Read evidence/verification-report.md and evidence/traceability-matrix.md
2. Note the Verified Commit hash from the QA report
3. Check traceability: run `git log --oneline | grep '{{requirementId}}'` to confirm commits reference this requirement
4. Create or update evidence/acceptance-verdict.md with a row for this requirement:

   | Requirement | Criteria Met | Evidence | Verdict |

   Include the verified commit hash and overall verdict (ACCEPTED / REJECTED)

If the QA verdict was PASS and at least one commit references {{requirementId}}, the verdict should be ACCEPTED.

5. FINAL STEP, do not skip: end the {{requirementId}} row or section in evidence/acceptance-verdict.md with this exact line on its own (the engine checks it):
   ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT {{requirementId}}: ACCEPTED
   or
   ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT {{requirementId}}: REJECTED
   Reject only for a gap in the product that the developer can fix, and say what the fix is. On ACCEPTED, the engine merges feature/{{requirementId}} into {{baseBranch}}.

exitEvaluation.prompt: Look at the ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT line you wrote for {{requirementId}} in evidence/acceptance-verdict.md. Is it exactly "ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT {{requirementId}}: ACCEPTED"? Answer with a single word: true or false.

onEntryCommands.reason: Discard uncommitted leftovers from a prior session so the checkout below cannot be blocked.
Fetch the latest remote branches pushed by other agents.
Check out the requirement's feature branch exactly as last pushed. It must already exist (created in REQUIREMENTS_DEFINITION).

onExitCommands.reason: Stage all new and modified files.
Commit staged changes with the requirement ID in the message, so traceability never depends on the LLM. No-op when nothing changed.
Capture the commit SHA for downstream traceability.
Push the feature branch so the next agent can check it out.

onExitCommands.command: R=evidence/acceptance-verdict.md; if grep -qE "ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT[[:space:]]+{{requirementId}}:[[:space:]]*\\**ACCEPTED" $R && ! grep -qE "ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT[[:space:]]+{{requirementId}}:[[:space:]]*\\**REJECTED" $R; then exit 0; fi; echo "Acceptance verdict for {{requirementId}} is not ACCEPTED. Verdict lines found:"; grep -n "ACCEPTANCE-VERDICT" $R || echo "(none)"; echo "See $R for the RA findings."; exit 1
onExitCommands.reason: Deterministic gate: merge only if the RA recorded an explicit ACCEPTED verdict line for this requirement. Runs after the push so the acceptance evidence is on the feature branch either way.

MERGING.name: Merge to Main
MERGING.description: Engine-only step (empty prompt: no LLM turn). Merges the accepted feature branch into {{baseBranch}} with a merge commit, pushes, and deletes the remote feature branch (the --no-ff merge commit keeps the branch history). A merge conflict or push failure escalates for human review rather than looping.

onEntryCommands.reason: Discard uncommitted leftovers from a prior session so the checkout below cannot be blocked.
Fetch the latest remote branches pushed by other agents.
Start from the latest {{baseBranch}}.
Merge the accepted feature branch. Fails on conflict, which escalates.
Capture the merge commit SHA for the audit trail.
Publish the merged {{baseBranch}}; the next requirement branches from it.
Delete the merged remote feature branch.

DONE.name: Complete
DONE.description: V-model complete: the requirement is accepted and merged into main. Terminal state.

ESCALATED.name: Escalated
ESCALATED.description: Failed after retries. Terminal state -- the failing agent logs escalation.
